_README: EMPTY SKELETON - this file ships unpopulated on purpose.
Rate bands are derived from one specific company's conversion economics and are
commercially confidential to that company. Nothing from a previous employer goes
in here. Generate your own.
HOW TO POPULATE:
1. Run references/refresh_queries.sql against your warehouse. It produces five
result sets: cohorts.json, geo_cells.json, drift.json, backtest.json and
snapshot_all.json.
2. Save each result set as JSON in one working directory.
3. python3 ../scripts/assemble_benchmarks.py <workdir> --date YYYY-MM-DD
4. Copy the regenerated benchmarks.json back over this file. Do NOT copy
creators_snapshot.json into version control - it is named-creator data and is
covered by .gitignore.
WHILE THIS FILE IS EMPTY the rate engine runs in advisory mode: it explains the
calculation and names the missing inputs, and refuses to print OPEN/TARGET/MAX.
See your profile rates.md and deals.md.
MINIMUM SAMPLE before a cohort is trusted: n >= 8 for a CPM band (a percentile of
a wide distribution), n >= 15 for a value rate (a ratio of sums, far more sensitive
to a single outlier). Both are configurable in assemble_benchmarks.py.
Anything left null below is a value the assembler computes. Anything marked TODO is
a decision a human has to make and write down.

bench.cpm.<level>.<cohort_key>.p25: 25th percentile of fee/views*1000 actually paid in this cohort
bench.cpm.<level>.<cohort_key>.p75: 75th percentile CPM paid - the top of the defensible band
bench.cpm.<level>.<cohort_key>.n: number of paid posts behind the band
bench.cpm.<level>.<cohort_key>.b_now_med: median CPM in the current regime period only - use to sanity-check drift
bench.cpm.<level>.<cohort_key>.b_now_n: sample size in the current regime period
bench.cpm.<level>.<cohort_key>.fee_med: median absolute fee, for the cases where views are missing

bench.value.<level>.<cohort_key>.r_cur: current-regime value per 1k views. THE number EV is built from
bench.value.<level>.<cohort_key>.rw: decay-weighted full-history value per 1k views (half-life 12 months)
bench.value.<level>.<cohort_key>.n_now: clean posts in the current regime period - drives the shrinkage weight
bench.value.<level>.<cohort_key>.s_cur: conversions per 1k views, same shrinkage treatment as r_cur
bench.value.<level>.<cohort_key>.value_per_conversion: cohort value per conversion - denominator of the creator-facing bar
bench.value.<level>.<cohort_key>.n: clean posts behind the value rate
bench.value.<level>.<cohort_key>.prof_window: share of clean posts where value within the payback window >= fee paid

levels.pnd: platform|niche|deliverable - most specific, preferred when n is sufficient
levels.d: deliverable across platforms - diagnostic only, not used for lookup

_schema.cohort_key_format: lowercase platform, then '|', then the niche string as stored in the CRM, then '|', then the normalised deliverable code

meta.value_basis: TODO - write the exact definition of the value column you summed, the attribution window, and whether promo-code conversions are allocated to in-window posts. Two companies using the same word here mean different things, and the difference lands directly in the walk-away ceiling.

rate_estimator.name: current-regime shrinkage
rate_estimator.r_now: current-regime pooled rate, mature posts only
rate_estimator.why: creator marketing goes through regime changes - conversion per view and views per dollar each move by multiples inside a year. Pure decay-weighting lags a regime change; a pure current-period rate is far too thin on small cohorts. Shrinkage buys the responsiveness of one and the stability of the other, and washes the prior out as n_now grows.

policy.anchor: median -> p75 of cohort CPM per negotiation doctrine

floors._note: TODO - fill from your profile rates.md ({{RATE_FLOOR_SHORTFORM}} / {{RATE_FLOOR_LONGFORM}}). These are policy, not model output: set each at roughly the fee below which a creator feels the production effort isn't worth it. The floor protects the relationship, not the budget.

meta.geo_note: T1 = 1.0 by design: cohort value rates are already T1-heavy, so T2/T3 act as discounts only. A cross-platform T1 uplift is deliberately NOT applied - it is dominated by whichever platform/tier combination has a near-zero-value view pool, and applying it would overstate T1 EV at cohort level.

auto_rules.promo_leak: TODO - absolute threshold AND share threshold, two-sided. Default shape: promo-only conversions >= A with promo share >= X%, OR >= B (much larger) with share >= Y%. Catches a code that escaped into coupon aggregators.
auto_rules.link_leak: TODO - absolute threshold AND rate threshold. Default shape: link conversions >= C at >= D per 1k views on social platforms. Catches a tracked link pasted somewhere it doesn't belong.
auto_rules.exceptional_converter: TODO - the band just below the link-leak rate. High but plausible = a retention priority, not a leak. Screen the ambiguous middle manually and record the verdict in `cleared`.

corpus._note: Sanity counters. If utm_join_rate drops between refreshes, the tracking convention changed and every value rate below is suspect - stop and fix the join before you publish a card.
